verses.126:1a: Se o Senhor não {aedif1} a casa, * em vão {laboraverunt} os que a {aedif2}.
verses.126:1b: Se o Senhor não guardar a cidade, * em vão {vigilat} o que a guarda.
verses.126:2a: {vanum} antes da luz: * levantai-vos {sederitis}, vós que comeis o pão da dor.
verses.126:2b: Quando ele der o sono aos seus amados: * {hereditas}: {merces}, o fruto do ventre.
verses.126:4: Como setas na mão do poderoso: * assim os filhos {excussorum}.
verses.126:5: Bem-aventurado o homem que {implevit} o seu desejo com eles: * não será envergonhado quando falar aos seus inimigos à porta.

decisions.latin: Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum … qui ædíficant eam
decisions.why: The Latin says one verb twice in one line, God's building and the builders' (οἰκοδομήσῃ … οἰκοδομοῦντες in the Greek too), and the line turns on it: the repetition stays (rule 2). *edificar* is the psalter's verb so far (50:20, 68:36, 77:69, 88:3, 88:5, 101:17, 121:3 — grep of the prayed files) and Matos Soares 1932's here. The CNBB Liturgia das Horas (fetched, `consult/web-lh-salmo-126-127.html`) and DM1962 say *construir … construtores*, and 117:22 has *os construtores* for the noun *ædificántes*; a Brazilian ear may know the line with *construir*. The moral sense of *edificar* ('edify') was heard once, at 121:3; here the object *a casa* closes it.

options.label: edificar … edificam
options.note: Ruling: the psalter's verb, both times; MS1932.

options.label: construir … constroem
options.note: The CNBB LH's verb (with the noun *construtores*) and DM1962's *construir*; plainer to the ear; breaks the row with 50:20, 68:36, 101:17, 121:3.

decisions.why: A perfect (Greek aorist ἐκοπίασαν) after a future-perfect condition: gnomic, or 'will have laboured'. Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 turn it into the present (*they labour in vain*; *é em vão que trabalham*). The Latin's perfect is kept: in Portuguese *em vão trabalharam* after *Se o Senhor não edificar* is heard as the result already sealed — the Latin's own logic — and the verb is *trabalhar*, as the *laboráre* row foresaw for this verse (48:9 *trabalhará*).

options.label: trabalharam
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's tense.

options.label: trabalham
options.note: DRB, MS1932: the gnomic sense as a present; matches 1b *vigia*.

options.label: trabalharão
options.note: The CNBB LH's future (from the Hebrew's perfect read as consequence).

decisions.why: *vigiláre* here is ἀγρυπνέω, to stay awake (the *vigiláre* row leaves 126:1b to be decided locally). *vigiar* keeps the Latin's word and is the row's verb (62:2a, 101:8); it says both watching and staying awake, and the watchman is named by the next words, *o que a guarda*. *frustra* → *em vão*, as 38:7 (*frustra* and *vane* are one Greek word, μάτην): here *in vanum*, *frustra* and *vanum est* are all εἰς μάτην, so the three are one Portuguese phrase (D15's test).

options.label: vigia
options.note: Ruling: the row's verb.

options.label: vela
options.note: Stays awake, the Greek's sense; but *velar* is heard with *velório*, as the row records at 101:8.

decisions.latin: Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere
decisions.why: The Latin predicates *vanum* of the infinitive, with a dative of the persons. Kept as it is built: *É vão para vós levantar*, so that the infinitive *súrgere* and the imperative *súrgite* are one verb in both cola (*levantar … levantai-vos*), as the Latin repeats it. Matos Soares 1932 makes it a finite verb (*Em vão vos levantais*), which asserts that they do rise — grammar, and allowed by D2, but the Latin only weighs the act. *ante lucem* → *antes da luz* (DRB 'before light', DM1962): the image kept, not *antes do amanhecer*.

options.label: É vão para vós levantar
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's build; 12 syllables on the Latin's 12.

options.label: Em vão vos levantais
options.note: MS1932's build; shorter, and echoes the *em vão* of 1a and 1b.

options.label: É em vão levantar-vos
options.note: The three *em vão* of the Greek audible, the infinitive kept; *vobis* folded into the reflexive.

decisions.why: The Latin has an imperative, *súrgite* (the Greek has a second infinitive, ἐγείρεσθαι μετὰ τὸ καθῆσθαι); the Latin is followed. *sedére* is to sit, and in the Vulgate family's reading to sit at rest: Matos Soares 1932 *depois que tiverdes repousado* (his note: they wear themselves out and despise God's help), Douay-Rheims 'after you have sitten'. The image of sitting is kept (rule 2: images stay, no explaining). The future perfect is carried by the compound infinitive *depois de vos terdes sentado*.

options.label: depois de vos terdes sentado
options.note: Ruling: the image and the tense.

options.label: depois de terdes repousado
options.note: MS1932: the sense of the sitting made explicit — explains (rule 2).

options.label: depois de estardes sentados
options.note: *sedére* as a state; can be heard as 'while you are seated'.

decisions.why: Verbless, with no article: *fílii* is apposition or predicate, and the Latin does not say which. *eis a herança do Senhor, os filhos* keeps the Latin's order and leaves both open; Douay-Rheims supplies a copula ('the inheritance of the Lord are children'), Matos Soares 1932 *Eis como herança do Senhor, os filhos*. *ecce → eis* (row), *heréditas → herança* (row). The clause *Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum* is left to run into it as DO's pointing has it; whether it closes 2a or opens 2b is left open, as in the Latin.

options.label: eis a herança do Senhor, os filhos

forms.hereditas: eis a herança do Senhor, os filhos

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order and openness.

options.label: eis que os filhos são a herança do Senhor

forms.hereditas: eis que os filhos são a herança do Senhor

options.note: DRB's copula, in natural order; closes the apposition as a predicate.

decisions.why: *merces* is wage, hire, reward (L&S; μισθός); only here in the psalter (grep; among the canticles, Isa 40:10, Eccli 36:18 and the canticle filed as Psalm255, 10:17). The Latin sets it in apposition to *fructus ventris* — the Greek has a genitive (ὁ μισθὸς τοῦ καρποῦ τῆς γαστρός, 'the reward of the fruit of the womb'); the Latin is followed. *recompensa* (MS1932, DRB 'reward') is the plain word; *salário* and *paga* are the wage and sound mercenary. The *retribúere* row uses *Recompensai* at 118:17 for another verb, in another psalm. *fructus ventris → o fruto do ventre* (*venter → ventre*, row), the words of the Ave Maria, which the Latin also shares.

options.label: a recompensa
options.note: Ruling.

options.label: o salário
options.note: The wage: the Latin's first sense, after the labour of 1a; heard as money.

options.label: o prêmio
options.note: DM1962's word (from the Hebrew); a prize rather than a due.

decisions.why: The crux of the psalm. *excússi* (ἐκτετιναγμένων) are 'those shaken out / off / cast out' — the Greek read the Hebrew's 'youth' (נְעוּרִים) as from a root 'to shake'. Who they are the Latin does not say: exiles shaken out of their land, the oppressed (Matos Soares 1932's *dos oprimidos*, an interpretation), or, in the Fathers' reading, those who have shaken off the world. Douay-Rheims keeps the image: 'the children of them that have been shaken'. Kept (rule 2), as a clause, because the bare participle *dos sacudidos* is not heard as persons. Cost: +4 syllables on the Latin's short colon.

options.label: dos que foram sacudidos
options.note: Ruling: DRB's wording; the image open.

options.label: dos sacudidos
options.note: The Latin's length; opaque.

options.label: dos expulsos
options.note: L&S 'cast out, drive out': the exiles' reading; closes the image to one sense.

options.label: dos oprimidos
options.note: MS1932: explains — refused (rule 2).

decisions.latin: qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis
decisions.why: *implére desidérium* is 'to fill / satisfy a desire' (πληρώσει τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν; the Hebrew's 'quiver' read as 'desire'). *encher* keeps the verb's own image, as 102:5 *Qui replet … desidérium tuum* → *enche … o teu desejo* already has it, and 128:7 *non implévit manum suam* will have *encher* with a hand. *ex ipsis → com eles* (DRB 'with them'): the sons, the arrows of 126:4 behind them. Matos Soares 1932's *viu cumprido o seu desejo acerca de tais filhos* explains.

options.label: encheu
options.note: Ruling: 102:5's verb.

options.label: cumpriu
options.note: The idiom for a desire in Portuguese; loses the filling (and the quiver behind it).

options.label: saciou
options.note: Satisfied; but *saciar* is satiáre's / saturáre's verb (102:5's decision).

choices.126:1a: No titulus: *Canticum graduum* (Salomonis) is not reproduced (D7; as Pss 119, 120, 133). *in vanum → em vão*; *domus → casa* (row).
choices.126:1b: *custodíre → guardar* (row), twice as the Latin has it (*custodíerit … custódit*). *frustra → em vão* (38:7).
choices.126:2a: *súrgere / súrgite → levantar / levantai-vos*: the Latin's one verb twice. *manducáre → comer* (row); *panis dolóris → o pão da dor* (MS1932; *dolor → dor*, row). *qui manducátis* → the vocative *vós que comeis*. The second colon is long, as the Latin's is (19 syllables).
choices.126:2b: *Cum déderit* → *Quando ele der*: the subject hidden in the verb named (D2); lowercase. *diléctis suis → aos seus amados* (the *diléctus* row; 59:7 *os vossos amados*). *somnus → sono*. Natural order puts *o sono* before the dative; the colon still ends on a paroxytone.
choices.126:4: *sagítta → seta* (row); *potens → o poderoso*, the row Ps 119:4 set up for this verse (*Setas agudas do poderoso*): God or a warrior left open. *in manu → na mão*. The Latin's verbless *ita* clause kept verbless (*assim os filhos …*); *assim são* would supply a copula.
choices.126:5: *Beátus vir → Bem-aventurado o homem* (D19). *confúndi → ser envergonhado* (D15); singular as the Latin (the Greek is plural). *loqui* + dative → *falar aos*; *in porta → à porta* (68:13: the city gate, where *na porta* is heard as 'in the doorway'). The second colon is a Vespers antiphon ([Daya3 Vespera], DO Psalmi major) *Non confundétur * cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta* and reads alone: *Não será envergonhado * quando falar aos seus inimigos à porta*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps126.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932, DM1962). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Liturgical uses by grep of DO Latin: 126 is the fourth psalm of Vespers of Our Lady (antiphons ;;126 at 07-02, 08-15t, 09-08, 10-11, 12-08, 02-11 and others, none cut from the psalm); two psalter antiphons from it in DO's Psalmi major — *Dóminus ædíficet * nobis domum, et custódiat civitátem* ([Day2 Vespera]; a paraphrase, not the psalm's wording) and *Non confundétur * cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta* ([Daya3 Vespera]). Brazilian circulation fetched, not asserted: the CNBB Liturgia das Horas text (Hebrew-based: *construir … construtores*, *sentinelas*, *flechas*, *aljava*, *junto às portas da cidade*) is saved in consult/web-lh-salmo-126-127.html and quoted in ps126/circulation.md. Hard readings: 126:4 *excussórum*; 126:2a *súrgite postquam sedéritis*; 126:2b the verbless apposition *heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris*; 126:5 *implévit desidérium … ex ipsis*.

v1: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft flags accepted (the counter does not elide): 126:2b first colon +4 (*ele* names the hidden subject, D2; *Quando der* alone could be heard as 'when I give') and second +4 (the Latin's four nouns and two articles Portuguese needs); 126:4 second colon +4 (the clause for *excussórum*, see the decision); 126:5 second colon +5 (*aos seus inimigos à porta* — every word is the Latin's; with elision nearer +3). 126:2a both cola end oxytone (*luz*, *dor*): allowed (stress on the last syllable). No rhyme flags.
